newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform saves 12 bln reais-CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform saves 12 bln reais-CNI.

text.p: A study by Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) shows that the current civil service reform bill in Congress would save 12 billion reais ($11.32 billion).

The CNI said the state would achieve savings amounting to 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) if the civil service reform bill were approved in its present form and the federal government, states and municipalities cut payroll costs to 60 percent of revenues.
The civil service reform bill is due to be voted in the Chamber of Deputies on April 2 and President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has promised to intervene personally to see the bill is approved.

It represents a powerful tool in the government's struggle to reduce public spending, but its main points -- an end to job guarantees for civil servants and a pay cap -- have met stiff resistance in Congress.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
